Then, on the night her brother vanished, a light came on in the house.

Mara ran through the rain and found the front door unlocked. Inside, dust lay thick over the furniture—except for a line of fresh footprints leading to the cellar. At the bottom of the stairs, beneath a bare bulb, stood a red wooden door. She had never seen it before.

She grabbed the handle. It burned her palm.
